sources.title: Cambodia Tourism Ministry's dated Chinese tourist trial announcement: October recheck
sources.publisher: Agence Kampuchea Presse, Ministry of Information, Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual complete government article dated 16 January 2026 reopened and read. Its operative paragraphs attribute the ordinary tourist trial to the Tourism Ministry's 15 January statement. AKP's separately reopened institutional article at https://akp.gov.kh/post/detail/354794 identifies it as the state-owned agency under the Ministry of Information. This fresh read establishes only the dated trial and its scope, not a successor.

sources.title: Cambodia trial launch and per-visit allowance: October recheck
sources.publisher: Agence Kampuchea Presse, Ministry of Information, Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual complete 15 June 2026 destination-government launch article reopened and read, including its express temporary endpoint and Tourism Minister's identified comments. The fourteen-day allowance applies only to the expired trial and is not republished as a current successor stay.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Eligible travellers will be permitted to stay for up to 14 days per visit

sources.title: Cambodia tourism meeting's private-sector extension request: October recheck
sources.publisher: Agence Kampuchea Presse, Ministry of Information, Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual complete 20 August 2026 government report reopened and read. The paragraphs describing the 4 August private-sector requests and the 19 August discussion distinguish an extension request from government adoption. The report is retained solely to prevent misreading the requested year-end extension as an operative successor.
sources.supportingExcerpt: the private sector raised two key requests

sources.title: PRC Embassy September holiday advisory: trial dates and alternative visa channels
sources.publisher: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Cambodia
sources.officialityEvidence: Actual complete advisory read on the official Chinese Embassy domain; visible publication stamp is 24 September 2026 despite the URL's 26 September path. Its first numbered section names ordinary PRC passports, repeats the trial dates and describes mission, online electronic and arrival visa channels for other travellers. This is passport-issuer corroboration, not destination-authority proof of a post-trial baseline for CN, HK or MO.

unresolved.reason: Post-trial ordinary tourist access from 16 October 2026 is not established by freshly accessible destination-authority evidence. Reopened AKP trial publications end on 15 October; the August report records an extension request, not adoption. The PRC Embassy's 24 September advisory mentions arrival and electronic visa channels outside the waiver, but it is issuer-side corroboration. Cambodia's eVisa service presented redirect loops or a browser-check page, its Paris mission visitor guidance now serves maintenance, and the London FAQ retains dated 2019/pandemic material. No current successor status, actual issuance timing or permitted stay is promoted from these incomplete reads.

Post-trial ordinary HKSAR tourist access from 16 October 2026 is not established by freshly accessible destination-authority evidence. Reopened AKP publications expressly include Hong Kong but limit the trial to 15 October; the year-end extension wording is a private-sector request. Current eVisa content could not be retrieved beyond a challenge, the Paris mission page is in maintenance, and London's 2019 exemption table is too stale to establish a successor. A specific arrival, electronic or prior-visa baseline and current stay allowance must not be inferred from the expired waiver, application availability or another PRC document.

Post-trial ordinary Macao SAR tourist access from 16 October 2026 is not established by freshly accessible destination-authority evidence. Reopened AKP publications expressly include Macao but end the trial on 15 October; the year-end extension wording is only a request. The government Macao June notice describes visa-on-arrival/eVisa availability before the trial and does not expressly establish its successor. Cambodia's eVisa challenge and the Paris mission's maintenance prevent a current destination-side route read. No successor status, issuance timing or stay is inferred from issuer guidance, expired trial scope or an application selector.
